自己表現は、自分だけではできない――self-expression is made of borrowed codes

Self-expression sounds like taking something already inside you and pushing it outward. But most of the materials are borrowed: language, clothing codes, music genres, emojis, platform formats. A totally private code becomes unreadable; pure conformity erases difference. This essay moves across self-presentation, extended self, cultural psychology, context collapse, and authenticity research to reframe self-expression as translation: placing a legible difference between self and others.
